To obtain valid net survival estimates, the population mortality should correctly reflect the expected mortality for each patient. The use of general life tables in the estimation of net survival for subgroups of the population with different overall mortality can lead to biased estimates of net survival. Estimation of net survival by deprivation is a situation where the use of general life tables can lead to overestimation of net survival in affluent groups, if these groups have a lower overall mortality than the general population, and the underestimation of net survival in the deprived groups, if these groups have a higher mortality than the general population \[[@CR33], [@CR34]\]. These questions arise also when stratifying by other factors that can influence overall mortality such as ethnicity \[[@CR35]\]. Conclusion {#Sec8} ========== In conclusion, this study has shown the existence of persistent socioeconomic inequalities in overall mortality in Portugal. texts.full_text: a village and civil parish in the English county of Staffordshire. It is within the borough of Stafford. The village describes itself as the Gateway to Cannock Chase, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Location It is located about four miles (6 km) south-east of Stafford town centre. Population The 2011 census recorded a population of 1,082 in 445 Households. The parish comes under the Stafford Non-Metropolitan District. Description The village is just outside the built-up area of Stafford, on the edge of Cannock Chase. The parish is one of the most affluent areas in Staffordshire, with a high proportion of detached houses and professional residents. The village itself is compact and centered around a small green and a popular gastropub called "The Olde Peculiar." History Brocton's history dates back to the Domesday Book, where it is mentioned as "Brocetone," meaning "farmstead by the brook." Over the centuries, Brocton has evolved from a small agricultural settlement to a residential village. The parish church, St. Peter's, dates back to the 12th century and features notable Norman architecture. Amenities Brocton offers several amenities, including a primary school, a village hall, and playing fields. The local cricket club is active during the summer months, and there are numerous walking and cycling routes that connect Brocton to the broader Cannock Chase area. The nearby Milford Common provides additional opportunities for outdoor recreation. Economy While primarily residential, some residents commute to Stafford, Birmingham, or other nearby urban areas for work. There is a small business park on the outskirts of the village that houses several local enterprises, including a popular garden center and a craft brewery. Transportation The village is well-connected by road, with easy access to the M6 motorway via junction 13 at Stafford. Public transportation includes regular bus services to Stafford town centre and other nearby villages. The nearest railway station is in Penkridge, approximately five miles away.
